title.narrative: Integrated agricultural and WASH lifesaving response to post-conflict needs of contested areas in Tselemti/West Telemt Woreda

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project is a multisectoral project designed to address the dire humanitarian needs of 63,262 conflict and drought-affected populations who have access to very limited to no humanitarian support in Tselemti/West Tselemt woreda. The project is designed and will be implemented by ZOA addressing the food insecurity and WASH service needs of internally displaced people, returnees, and host communities in the area. Agriculture: This project aims to tackle food insecurity by supporting smallholder farmers with access to improved drought-resistant seeds and restocking interventions. To combat drought effects and promote year-round production, we will rehabilitate conflict-damaged irrigation schemes. We also plan to implement restocking intervention through distributing small ruminants and poultry for dietary diversification and income generation. The livestock sector has been heavily impacted by recent conflicts and droughts, leading to limited access to animal health services. This project will provide mass vaccination and address equipment gaps in animal health centers, while strengthening the capacity of government development agents in the area. WASH: To enhance access to safe water and sanitation, the project will rehabilitate water points, repair facilities, construct waste disposal pits, promote hygiene practices, etc. A gender-balanced WASH committee (at least 50% women) will be established and trained for project management. To meet urgent needs, essential WASH non-food items and MHM dignity kits will be distributed. The intervention will collaborate closely with local community representatives and relevant government offices. The expected outcomes of the intervention include increased agricultural productivity and food security improved access to safe water and sanitation services strengthened community resilience and self-reliance and enhanced knowledge and skills among community members. Intersectoral collaboration and localization: To avoid duplication of efforts and ensure synergy and coordination, ZOA will ensure this project’s coordination with its ongoing WASH and Food Security and Livelihoods with ASDEPO-led Health and Nutrition intervention and others with similar interventions. By collaborating closely with and enhancing the capacity of local government bodies and community representatives, the project will empower local communities to actively participate in decision-making processes and drive their development. This participatory approach ensures that interventions are tailored to specific community needs and promotes ownership and sustainability. AAP: Through adopting a comprehensive monitoring and evaluation AAP and monitoring system, risk management framework, and installing locally tailored compliant and feedback response mechanisms, ZOA will ensure that AAPs are enhanced. A community-level appeal committee will ensure a swift response to any concerns. Inclusion and protection mainstreaming: the project will ensure the participation of targeted vulnerable communities in the project decision-making processes. Protection will be mainstreamed across all WASH and agriculture interventions to ensure safe and dignified access to project services to the project targets, especially to the most vulnerable community groups. Localization: ZOA's strong commitment to localization, coupled with its experience and collaborative approach (e.g.close collaboration with our local partner, ASDEPO and other actors in the area) positions this project to effectively address the humanitarian crisis in Tselemti/West Telemt and contribute to building long-term community resilience. Additionally, by prioritizing gender and disability inclusion, the project will ensure that the needs of women, girls, and people with disabilities are addressedltbrgtlt/pgt
